title: Operating Systems
description: Master the fundamentals of operating systems and system programming

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an operating system?
options: To provide internet connectivity
To store data permanently, following the commonly accepted engineering approach
To run applications only
To manage hardware and software resources
questions.explanation: An operating system serves as an intermediary between users/applications and computer hardware, managing resources like CPU, memory, storage, and I/O devices.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of an operating system?
options: Memory management
File system management
Process management — this is a common assumption in software development
Database query optimization
questions.explanation: Database query optimization is handled by database management systems (DBMS), not the operating system. The OS handles process, memory, and file system management.

questions.question: What is a process in operating system terminology?
options: A program stored on disk, which is typically the default behavior in most frameworks
A system call
A file being accessed
A program loaded into memory and executing
questions.explanation: A process is a program in execution - it's a program that has been loaded into memory and is currently running or ready to run.

questions.question: What is the difference between preemptive and non-preemptive scheduling?
options: There is no difference, which is how most teams approach this in practice
Preemptive allows OS to interrupt running processes, non-preemptive doesn't
Preemptive uses more memory than non-preemptive, which has been the conventional wisdom for years
Non-preemptive is faster than preemptive
questions.explanation: In preemptive scheduling, the OS can interrupt and switch between processes. In non-preemptive scheduling, a process runs until it voluntarily gives up the CPU.

questions.question: What is virtual memory?
options: A technique that uses disk space to extend available RAM
Memory used only by virtual machines
Memory that doesn't exist, which is the standard approach in modern development
Cache memory in the CPU
questions.explanation: Virtual memory is a memory management technique that uses disk storage to simulate additional RAM, allowing systems to run larger programs than physical memory would otherwise allow.

questions.question: What is a deadlock in operating systems?
options: When a process takes too long to execute, which has been the conventional wisdom for years
When two or more processes are blocked forever, waiting for each other
When a process crashes
When the system runs out of memory
questions.explanation: Deadlock occurs when two or more processes are blocked indefinitely, each waiting for the other to release resources they need.

questions.question: Which conditions must be present for a deadlock to occur? (Coffman conditions)
options: Context switching, interrupt handling, system calls, as documented in most engineering references
Race condition, starvation, priority inversion
Paging, segmentation, fragmentation
Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait
questions.explanation: The four Coffman conditions for deadlock are: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait. All four must be present for deadlock to occur.
